note: v1936: The last unswept class from the hardening brief: a comment asserting a rule the adjacent code does not enforce. The broad sweep is useless and saying so IS the finding - matching strong assertions above code returned 449 candidates and every one inspected was ordinary prose using never descriptively, which is a finding too large to act on and therefore noise. The one real instance came from following a known scar instead: the chronicle still-threshold constant is 0.002, while the calibration table three lines above it still read 0.005 chosen. A later version had moved the constant correctly with its evidence immediately below, and nobody updated the table above - two statements about one number, three lines apart, disagreeing. Nothing was broken because the code is right; what was broken is the instruction to the next reader, who sees the old value marked chosen beside the new one and helpfully corrects a deliberate decision back to the comment. I nearly did exactly that, which is the only reason it is written down. The guard own first draft used an io helper in a suite that does not import io, so the guard about stale comments failed on its own missing import.
